concerns.text: The plan applies a *deterministic synthetic‑label distribution* (hydrolysis 60 %, oxidation 30 %, photolysis 10 %) when degradation pathway labels are missing (see step 4). These synthetic labels are generated without any reference to the molecular structure, yet the downstream validation (macro‑F1 performance, Integrated Gradients attribution, χ² motif significance) treats them as ground‑truth. This creates a circular validation: the model is evaluated against labels that are not independent of the predictor, allowing trivial learning of class priors rather than true structure‑to‑mechanism relationships.

Integrated Gradients validation (step 9) requires that for *hydrolysis* cases the ester bond appears in the top 90 % of attribution scores. When the hydrolysis labels are synthetic (as per the deterministic distribution), the expectation that the ester bond is important is imposed a‑priori, making the attribution test tautological. The same issue applies to the χ² test (step 10) which evaluates motif importance derived from a model trained on synthetic, structure‑agnostic labels; the statistical significance therefore does not reflect a genuine structure‑mechanism association.

Data augmentation verification (task T014b) only checks row‑count and edge‑drop proportion, but does not confirm that the augmented graphs retain chemically valid substructures. Without such verification the augmentation could introduce artefacts that the GNN learns, compromising the scientific validity of any reported performance.
